transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - Clearmed), Jonas Park (Lead ML Eng), Aimee Liu (SRE)
Shared artifacts: slide deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/clearmed-onramp), sample benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/clearmed-sample)

00:00 Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we have about 45 minutes ish, we'll run a quick hosted API demo, show the Console a bit, and then Diego will jump into Optimize recommendations for cost/latency.
00:12 Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. Quick ask before we start — we have some folks in EU who need data residency info, I put Aimee on for the SRE questions.
00:20 Maya: Great, noted. We'll hit the security bit during the Q&A. Diego, wanna kick the demo?
00:26 Diego: Yep. I'll share my screen — is that visible?
:30 (screen share noise)
00:34 Diego: Alright first thing — hosted chat endpoint. We'll do a live run of a simple assistant conversation using streaming. The basic call is the /v1/chat/completions style route, we stream tokens.
00:52 Jonas: Quick question — in your docs you mention automatic prefix caching, how does that work for chat histories?
01:01 Diego: Good one. So we do prefix/KV cache — basically when the same conversation context is reused the model doesn't recompute earlier tokens; the KV cache is keyed by model version and conversation prefix. Sometimes our transcription shows it as "K-V cash" in internal logging, haha, but it's a KV cache.
01:20 Priya: Does that preserve residency? Like if KV cache is in region X, can we pin it?
01:27 Diego: Yes, for private and dedicated you can pin; for hosted we have region routing — requests from eu-west-1 will hit eu nodes and the cache is in-region. We'll send the architecture note.
01:42 Maya: I'm going to run a quick generation, you'll see tokens stream in. This is with default parameters — temperature 0.7, max_tokens 150.
01:50 (typing)
02:05 Diego: You'll notice streaming latency is sub-200ms per chunk for short responses in this demo model — your real latencies will depend on sequence length and model.
02:14 Aimee: What's the difference between streaming chunk size and the total token throughput?
02:20 Diego: Chunk size is largely the SDK/transport behavior — the runtime batches token generation. We expose a few knobs: chunk interval hints, and the runtime will try to emit partial tokens as soon as they're available. For throughput, batching across requests improves GPU utilization.
02:34 Jonas: Do you recommend batching on our side or relying on Redwood's automatic batching?
02:40 Diego: Both. For unpredictable traffic patterns, Redwood's continuous batching helps. But if you can buffer similar requests you can get better p50 and cost. Optimize will suggest a batching window based on your histogram.
03:00 Maya: Quick aside — if anyone sees typos in the transcript later blame our ASR, it turns "KMS" into "K-M-S" sometimes.
03:06 (laugh)
03:12 Priya: On retries — we saw in our tests with another provider that retry storms cause spikes. How do you recommend implementing client retries?
03:22 Diego: We advise exponential backoff with jitter, and idempotency keys where possible. For streaming you want to make the call idempotent at the message level — include an idempotency token for message replays. Redwood also has server-side fallbacks — if a model variant is overloaded we can route to a compatible smaller variant, and we surface that in the response metadata.
03:50 Jonas: Metadata, ok. Is that returned in headers?
03:54 Diego: It shows up in response envelope — we put route/model and whether it was a fallback; SDKs also surface it as part of the response object.
04:10 Maya: I'm going to show the Console — Diego if you want to pull up per-route dashboards?
04:17 Diego: Yep. Console: top-level you can see token spend, per-route latency percentiles, error rates, and a breakdown by model variant. Here's a route we instrumented for a support chatbot — you can see p50/p95 and a token cost curve.
04:40 Aimee: Can we get per-token cost by user or API key?
04:45 Diego: Yes, token-level billing can be correlated to keys and routes — Console has a filter to show cost per API key and tag. For enterprise customers we can emit more granular logs to your logging endpoint.
04:58 Priya: Do you keep raw transcripts? Our privacy policy forbids persistent storage of raw PII from chats.
05:05 Maya: By default we retain logs for 30 days in hosted, but you can change retention and opt for no retention; for enterprise/Private we can disable retention and route logs to your KMS-protected bucket. We'll send the SOC2 + retention policy.
05:20 Priya: Good. KMS — do you integrate with our KMS/HSM?
05:23 Diego: Yes, via customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we use our KMS but can integrate for key wrapping on request (enterprise plan).
05:33 Jonas: Back on performance — you mentioned quantization suggestions in Optimize. Are those automated or manual?
05:41 Diego: Optimize recommends quantization knobs per model and workload. For example, 4-bit or 8-bit profiles where accuracy loss is small. We show an eval delta chart in the Console — you can roll out a quantized variant, traffic split it, and monitor quality regressions.
05:59 Maya: I'm switching to a live quick prompt that includes a function call to test structured output — we'll show function calling and streaming together.
06:08 (typing)
06:18 Diego: The assistant triggers a function and the console shows structured payloads in the per-route trace. Note: our ASR sometimes prints "function calling" as "function callingg" in the auto-summary, ignore typos.
06:36 Priya: Does function calling change tokenization or cost?
06:40 Diego: The modeling cost is the same; the structured payload may add a few tokens. We also have a reranking endpoint if you want to generate N candidates and pick best via rerank — more control at higher cost.
06:58 Jonas: For streaming failures — if a stream drops mid-response, do you recommend re-requesting whole message or a resumable approach?
07:07 Diego: Currently we recommend re-request with the idempotency token and to include client-side logic to stitch partials if you cache the last partial. We're working on formal resumable streams but it's not generally supported yet — would require stronger KV-level checkpoints.
07:25 Aimee: Any built-in rate limiting? We need per-API-key quotas and burst limits; how does that handle retries?
07:32 Maya: Yes, Redwood enforces per-key rate limits and a graceful 429 policy. We also expose rate-limit headers so clients can back off before hitting hard limits.
07:44 Priya: Could you show Optimize's recommendation view?
07:48 Diego: Sure — Optimize will ingest a sample of your workloads (we provided a sample upload UI) and produce recommendations: batching window suggestions, cache TTLs for prefix caching, and model quantization candidates. It also simulates cost delta vs latency. Here's an example: for session-based chat we suggested a 60ms batching window with max-batch-size 32 for our customer's traffic pattern.
08:20 Jonas: That feels risky for latency-sensitive UI. If p95 jumps, can we do canary rollouts?
08:26 Diego: Absolutely — Console has rollout controls: canary percentage, automatic rollback on quality or latency breach, and route-level fallbacks to the previous model.
08:38 Maya: We ran a small test earlier that shows a drop in unit cost by ~28% with small batch + quantization for a knowledge-base summarizer. I'll paste the benchmark link in the chat.
08:49 (link posted)
08:53 Priya: On compliance — do you have SOC2 type II?
08:56 Maya: Yes, we do SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO docs for customers upon NDA.
09:02 Aimee: For SSO, SAML or OIDC?
09:05 Maya: Both SAML and OIDC are supported for Console. RBAC supports team-level roles and route-level permissioning.
09:13 Jonas: Can we export traces? We want to forward them to our ELK stack.
09:18 Diego: You can enable forwarding of audit logs, traces and request/response metadata to your logging endpoint. We redact PII by default but can adjust per contract.
09:30 Priya: Pricing — send us the hosted pricing and any uplift for enterprise features?
09:34 Maya: Will do. We have usage pricing plus a flat fee for the enterprise add-ons (longer retention, KMS integration, dedicated support). I'll include a spreadsheet that models latency vs cost tradeoffs.
09:49 Jonas: Aimee will likely run the benchmark — SRE side. We'll probably want a controlled 2-hour window that mimics our 100 RPS load pattern.
09:57 Diego: Perfect. I'll prepare the script and a sample Prometheus dashboard you can plug into.
10:06 (brief pause)
10:10 Priya: One more thing — data residency specifics: certain clinical PII must never leave eu-west-1. Can you guarantee that on hosted?
10:20 Maya: For hosted, requests originating from eu region are routed in-region; we can provide a region-locked tenancy for EU enterprise customers. For hard guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private, but most customers do region routing + contractual SLAs. We'll follow up with a short note outlining options.
10:38 Jonas: If we start hosted and later want Dedicated, what's the migration path?
10:42 Diego: We support pinning model versions and exporting route configs. Migration typically involves provisioning Dedicated capacity, importing your routes and API keys, and running a short sync; we help with cutover plans.
10:58 Aimee: Any caveats about model version pinning? If you pin an older variant, do you miss security patches?
11:04 Diego: Good question. Pinning a model version pins the weights and inference binary; security patches to the control plane are still applied. We recommend periodic model upgrades and we provide a compatibility matrix.
11:20 Maya: We're about 38 minutes in, let's do a quick recap and next steps.
11:25 Priya: Sounds good.
11:27 Maya: Recap — we demoed hosted chat streaming, Console per-route observability, and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization/cache. Action items: Diego will send load test script and sample dashboards. I'll send pricing, SOC2 and retention docs. Priya will confirm EU residency list and security contact.
11:45 Priya: I'll gather our list and loop in legal for the SOC2 request.
11:50 Jonas: For the benchmark let's aim next Tuesday morning, that works on our side.
11:54 Maya: I'll put tentative calendar invites after the call. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
11:58 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears: "K-V cash" for "KV cache", "function callingg" typos in auto-summary. Speaker attribution sometimes generic in auto-exports.
